description: Tacos al Pastor are a true culinary icon of Mexico, featuring thinly sliced pork marinated in a vibrant blend of chiles and spices, then traditionally cooked on a vertical spit. The meat is slowly roasted, creating tender, flavorful layers with crispy edges, ready to be shaved off and served in warm tortillas. This recipe brings the authentic taste of the taqueria right to your home, promising a feast for the senses.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chile Marinade
instructions.text: Start by rehydrating the guajillo and ancho chiles. Place them in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them soak for about 20 minutes until softened. Once soft, drain the chiles and remove any remaining stems and seeds. In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, achiote paste, peeled garlic cloves, roughly chopped white onion, pineapple juice, white vinegar, cumin powder, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Blend until you achieve a very smooth paste. Add a tablespoon or two of water if needed to help the blending process.

instructions.title: Marinate the Pork
instructions.text: Take your thinly sliced pork shoulder and place it in a large bowl or a resealable bag. Pour the prepared chile marinade over the pork, ensuring every slice is thoroughly coated. Massage the marinade into the meat. Cover the bowl or seal the bag and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to deeply penetrate the pork.

instructions.title: Assemble the Trompo
instructions.text: Once the pork is marinated, it is time to assemble your trompo. If using a vertical spit, thread the marinated pork slices onto the spit, layering them tightly to form a cone shape. Place a thick slice of fresh pineapple at the base and top of the pork cone. The pineapple helps keep the meat moist and adds flavor. If you do not have a vertical spit, you can stack the pork slices on skewers and cook horizontally on a rotisserie.

instructions.title: Spit Grill the Al Pastor
instructions.text: Preheat your vertical spit grill or rotisserie to a medium-high heat. Place the assembled trompo onto the grill. The cooking time will vary depending on the size of your trompo and the heat of your grill, typically ranging from 1 to 2 hours. Rotate the meat slowly, allowing it to cook evenly and develop crispy, caramelized edges. The internal temperature of the pork should reach 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

instructions.title: Carve and Prepare for Tacos
instructions.text: As the outer layers of the al pastor cook and crisp up, carefully shave thin slices of meat directly from the trompo using a sharp knife. Continue to cook and shave the meat as needed. You can also dice the shaved meat into smaller pieces if preferred. Keep the shaved meat warm while you prepare the tortillas.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve Your Tacos
instructions.text: Warm your small corn tortillas on a comal or a dry skillet until pliable and slightly toasted. For each taco, place a generous portion of the freshly carved al pastor meat onto a warm tortilla. Garnish with finely diced white onion, chopped fresh cilantro, and a small piece of grilled pineapple from the trompo. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the tacos. Enjoy the authentic taste of Mexico!

tips: For truly authentic flavor, seek out Mexican oregano, which has a distinct citrusy and earthy profile different from Mediterranean oregano. It makes a noticeable difference in the marinade.
When assembling your trompo, ensure the pork slices are tightly packed. This helps the meat cook evenly and retain moisture, preventing it from drying out on the spit.

To keep the shaved al pastor meat warm and juicy while serving, you can place it in a tortilla warmer or a covered dish. Offer a variety of salsas, from mild to fiery, for guests to customize their tacos.
